doc.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Anxious moment with Gunther Schuller and the celeste
summary: Playing celeste in a Webern piece with Orchestra USA.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Oh well, I wanted to ask you a little bit about Gunther Schuller.
Oh yeah I was involved with him. Yeah if I had to pick highlights, and interesting experiences, and you ask me about a — what was it, an anxiety-producing – what was that question?
Yes. Well I called it — I forget what I called it. I can’t remember now. An anxious moment.

Oh yes, we’ve all had many anxious moments. But one, a lot of them involved John Lewis, but well I had anxious moments with Gunther. These are musical things. Well I was involved in the Orchestra USA. One time we had to play a Webern piece. See we were playing all kinds of music. And I’m not really classical, and I had to play the celeste. And this was one of those times where, like the guy with the cymbal, you just count until your — it was just a few little notes I had to play in this spot in this Webern piece. I was an absolute nervous wreck waiting, if I was going to make it, counting all these bars in this complicated, Gunther — and he practically stood over me, he kind of practically did it for me and I made it. It was a very anxious moment.
I know what you mean. Those orchestra things, man, 86 measures — I’m a saxophone player.

So you know on occasion when there’s a saxophone part in an orchestra, you’re waiting and waiting, and you say I hope to God he gives me a cue because I lost it and I hope it’s the right cue. And it’s always a solo, of course, after waiting all that time.
